correctness.rationale: For one nonconstant cyclic binary word, each t≥1 transition pair count yields t positive 0-runs and t positive 1-runs, forcing 2t≤n and allowing all A∈[0,n−2t] through 0^(A+1)1^(B+1)(01)^(t−1). Constant cycles give exactly A=0 or n. Summing independent integer intervals over active cycles plus zero-constant subset sums establishes the iff characterization, with explicit witnesses. For T≥r distribute T−r among all capacities floor(n_i/2)−1 so all cycles active and full A-layer results; all 2-length strands show sharp failure at T=r−1. For r=2 direct T=0,1,≥2 layer counting gives exact formula, including equal-length missing A=n1−1. Independent exhaustive enumeration of both-cycle word pairs for 2≤n1,n2≤7 agrees; analytic run decomposition is all-length proof.
